OAC S3 capture busy turn: write a numbered list of 40 distinct one-sentence facts about lighthouses. Do not use any tools.

item.text:
1. A lighthouse is a tower or other structure that emits light to help guide vessels.
2. Lighthouses warn sailors about hazards such as reefs, shoals, and rocky coastlines.
3. A lighthouse’s light can also help mariners identify their location.
4. The light-producing apparatus inside a lighthouse is called a lantern.
5. Many traditional lighthouses used a Fresnel lens to concentrate light into a powerful beam.
6. Fresnel lenses use rings of glass to bend light while weighing less than a comparable solid lens.
7. A lighthouse’s characteristic flash pattern is called its light characteristic.
8. Mariners can distinguish some lighthouses by the timing and color of their flashes.
9. A lighthouse’s height affects how far its light can be seen over the horizon.
10. Fog can block a lighthouse beam, so some lighthouses also have sound signals.
11. A foghorn warns nearby vessels when visibility is poor.
12. Some lighthouses use bells or sirens as fog signals.
13. Many lighthouses were built on islands or headlands to improve their visibility.
14. Offshore lighthouses may stand on reefs, rocks, or submerged shoals.
15. Lighthouse foundations are designed to resist waves, wind, and erosion.
16. Some lighthouse towers are made of stone, while others are made of brick, iron, or concrete.
17. A lighthouse’s painted bands or patterns can help sailors recognize it by day.
18. The distinctive daytime appearance of a lighthouse is called its daymark.
19. A lighthouse can be automated, removing the need for a resident keeper.
20. Before automation, lighthouse keepers maintained the light and its equipment.
21. Keepers often had to climb stairs to reach the lantern room.
22. Some lighthouses include living quarters for their keepers and families.
23. Lighthouse stairs may spiral around a central column.
24. A lighthouse’s lamp may be mounted on a rotating mechanism to create flashes.
25. Some modern lighthouses use LEDs instead of traditional oil or incandescent lamps.
26. Solar panels can supply electricity to lighthouses in remote locations.
27. Lighthouses are aids to navigation, but they do not steer ships or guarantee safe passage.
28. Mariners use charts and other navigation aids alongside lighthouse signals.
29. The International Association of Marine Aids to Navigation and Lighthouse Authorities assigns many lighthouse identifiers.
30. Some lighthouses are listed on nautical charts with details about their light and location.
31. Lighthouse keepers historically used oil lamps before electric lighting became common.
32. The first known lighthouse at Alexandria stood near the entrance to Egypt’s ancient harbor.
33. The Lighthouse of Alexandria was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
34. The Tower of Hercules in Spain is an ancient Roman lighthouse that remains in use.
35. Lighthouse museums often preserve lenses, lamps, and keepers’ records.
36. Some disused lighthouses have been converted into museums or visitor attractions.
37. Lighthouses may be threatened by coastal erosion and rising seas.
38. A lighthouse’s visible range is sometimes called its nominal range.
39. The brightness of a light and atmospheric conditions affect how far it can be seen.
40. Lighthouse designs vary to suit local geography, weather, and navigation needs.
